title: One status. Two very different next moves.
lede: The amount is unchanged. The decision word is not.
review_question: Which source record authorizes the status shown to the customer?

impact.person: A person may choose to wait, appeal, or contact support based on the status they see.
impact.workflow: A queue may close or reopen the case if it consumes the summary as a final state.
impact.industry: Service providers could request source-linked evidence for status changes; buyer demand is untested.
impact.market: If status feeds vendor or risk reporting, the label could affect comparisons. No pricing or trading is simulated.
impact.long_tail: If the summary is copied into dashboards and later reports, one uncorrected label could travel. Each link needs real provenance to establish that chain.

title: A green sentence over a red receipt.
lede: A status summary changes the reported test outcome while the release number stays fixed.
source: Release 4: 2 checks failed. Deployment status: blocked.
candidate: Release 4: 2 checks passed. Deployment status: approved.
review_question: Can the original test receipt and the summary be joined by release ID and timestamp?

impact.person: A user could be exposed to a change earlier than expected if a release decision relied on the altered summary.
impact.workflow: An operator might skip a review gate if a narrative status disagrees with the check receipt.
impact.industry: Teams can use this as a concrete source-to-summary regression fixture, not as certification of a release system.
impact.market: If deployments affect a paid service, reliability and customer confidence may be downstream concerns; no actual incident is asserted.
impact.long_tail: A status copied across tickets, dashboards, and postmortems can create a durable but false history unless each copy retains provenance.

title: The headline improves. The sample did not.
lede: An intentionally fictional trading-study summary changes both a count and a result word.
source: SIMULATION ONLY: 18 of 240 sample trades failed; signal remains unapproved.
candidate: SIMULATION ONLY: 6 of 240 sample trades passed; signal approved.
review_question: What are the underlying records, definitions, and sample-selection rules?

impact.person: A reader could mistake an edited simulation summary for evidence about their own financial decisions.
impact.workflow: A research reviewer can locate changed counts and curated status words before relying on the memo.
impact.industry: Evaluation teams could test whether source-linked reviews catch this class of edit; this fixture is not an accuracy benchmark.
impact.market: If research summaries are shared or aggregated, changed figures may alter perceptions. This is not live market data, a forecast, or a trading signal.
impact.long_tail: When a summary becomes an input to other summaries, provenance and version lineage determine whether an early discrepancy can still be found.

title: The checklist shows its own blank spaces.
lede: A checklist can surface questions that the supplied excerpt does not answer; it cannot fill them in.
candidate: We may retain support logs to improve reliability. An analyst may inspect submitted incidents. We do not use logs to train the public model.
review_question: Where do the complete terms specify duration, deletion, recipients, and opt-out?

impact.person: A customer can ask for the relevant policy text instead of treating this short excerpt as the whole policy.
impact.workflow: A procurement reviewer can route unmatched checklist fields for document-level review.
impact.industry: A shared checklist could make vendor comparisons more repeatable, but the field matches are keyword cues—not legal analysis.
impact.market: Clearer disclosures might affect a buyer's evaluation; this demo makes no claim about vendor ranking or market demand.
impact.long_tail: If a checklist is mistaken for a completeness guarantee, omitted clauses may disappear from later summaries. The UI labels each no-match as excerpt-scoped.

title: Two alphabets. One invisible separator.
lede: The scan exposes a Cyrillic character and a zero-width format control in a synthetic string.
candidate: Submitted token: pаyload; hidden separator: admin​istrator.
review_question: Does the downstream system normalize, compare, display, or authorize this exact sequence of code points?

impact.person: A reader may not see why two visually similar strings behave differently in a particular system.
impact.workflow: Engineers can inspect the exact code points and test their own parser or renderer.
impact.industry: Unicode handling can be a useful test dimension for text-processing pipelines; this census does not establish exploitability.
impact.market: A downstream account or transaction impact would depend on a vulnerable system and verified exploit path, neither of which is shown here.
impact.long_tail: When normalized text is hashed, indexed, or compared across services, differing normalization rules can split the evidence trail. Verify each boundary.

title: A term is not a complete agreement.
lede: The frame ledger maps matched words and leaves unmatched fields explicitly unresolved.
candidate: License: perpetual, non-exclusive internal use. We may sublicense. Either party may terminate after written notice. Liability is capped at fees paid.
review_question: Read the full agreement and governing context; do not treat a cue ledger as legal advice.

impact.person: A creator or buyer can identify terms to locate in the full agreement before making a decision.
impact.workflow: A reviewer can triage duration, sublicense, termination, remedy, jurisdiction, and liability language.
impact.industry: A repeatable cue map may help teams compare documents; it does not determine rights or replace counsel.
impact.market: Contract terms can shape commercial options, but this snippet does not establish value, enforceability, or negotiation leverage.
impact.long_tail: If a cue checklist is detached from the full document, a partial view can acquire false authority; retain the source and section context.

title: An alternative is generated—not recovered.
lede: The tool can produce a bounded lexical variation and label it as an illustration, never as hidden intent.
candidate: We may retain 30-day diagnostics to improve reliability.
review_question: Which text is quoted evidence, and which text was generated only to explore a contrast?

impact.person: A reader can compare wording without being told that a machine has discovered what someone meant.
impact.workflow: A facilitator can use a clearly marked counterfactual to ask which source wording matters.
impact.industry: Labeling generated alternatives can make creative analysis auditable; it does not prove the alternative is exhaustive or semantically equivalent.
impact.market: No inference about a product, company, or market is made from the generated variation.
impact.long_tail: If an illustration is later copied without its label, it can be mistaken for evidence. The artifact keeps provenance visible beside the transformation.

title: One failing authorization check disappears.
lede: A synthetic test receipt contradicts a draft audit summary; neither proves that a live contract is exploitable.
source: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — AUTH-04: unauthorized caller invoked transfer. Test: failed. Critical findings: 1. Release status: blocked.
candidate: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE — Draft audit summary: AUTH-04: unauthorized caller did not invoke transfer. Test: passed. Critical findings: 0. Release status: approved.
review_question: Can the test run, contract revision, network, and reviewer decision be joined to this draft summary?

impact.person: A developer or customer could rely on an unsupported summary; this fixture says nothing about a live exploit or actual loss.
impact.workflow: A release decision could diverge if reviewers follow the narrative but do not inspect the versioned authorization test.
impact.industry: Audit teams can test whether findings stay traceable to code revisions and test receipts; this is not a security certification.
impact.market: If verified evidence informs a release or risk disclosure, it could affect confidence. No real protocol, investment, or market effect is asserted.
impact.long_tail: A summary copied into later audit records can detach a claim from its failed test. Establish real propagation with identifiers, timestamps, and source records.

title: Same numbers. Different assignments. No cue fired.
lede: A deliberate role swap keeps the number multiset and polarity words unchanged—a visible miss, not a pass.
review_question: Can an external schema or row-level comparison bind each count to its category?

impact.person: A reviewer who sees only a green status may miss a changed allocation between categories.
impact.workflow: This case demonstrates why equal totals and word-presence checks cannot replace structured field comparison.
impact.industry: A credible evaluation should include known misses, not only examples the tool catches.
impact.market: If role-swapped counts feed a public report or internal risk model, conclusions could change. This demo does not claim such a system exists.
impact.long_tail: A quiet miss can survive several layers of summarization. Record the schema, source rows, and downstream consumers to test the real risk.
